en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: Course provides introduction to computer networks and in detail describes protocol architecture according to individual reference model layers.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Introduction to computer networks (allowance 2/2) a.provided servicesb.conceptsc.network securityd.current trends2.Network operating systems (allowance 2/2) a.for end devices and intermediate devicesb.OS typesc.command syntaxd.basic configuration of network devices3.Network protocols and princple of communication (allowance 2/2) a.reference models TCP/IP and ISO/OSIb.network protocols encapsulation4.Physical network media and signal transmission (allowance 2/2) a.metallic, optic and wireless network mediab.coding and modulationc.methods for media access control5.Ethernet (allowance 4/4) a.specificationb.frame structurec.switching principled.ARP protocol6.Network layer protocols (allowance 2/2) a.IPv4 and IPv6, their header structureb.routing principlesc.basic configuration of router7.IP addressing (allowance 2/2) a.structure of IPv4 addressb.network maskc.IPv4 and IPv6 address for special purposesd.ICMP protocol8.Address space design (allowance 4/4) a.classfull and classless IPv4 addressingb.subnettingc.design of IPv4 and IPv6 addressing9.Transport layer protocols (allowance 2/2) a.TCP and UDPb.ensuring reliability using TCP protocol10.Application layer (allowance 4/4) a.HTTP(S)b.e-mail (SMTP, IMAP, POP3)c.DNSd.DHCPe.Telnetf.SSHg.FTPh.TFTP11.Design of small size network (allowance 2/2) a.network design and its conceptsb.ensuring securityc.troubleshooting in small size network
